research.website_note: The results identify transistor.fm as Transistor’s official site and include its company, product, and customer pages.
research.gaps: Current pricing details and the present status of the video-podcast rollout are not specified.

strategy.observation: Transistor already powers branded podcasts for companies including Kit.com.
strategy.offer_link: A referral partnership could give Transistor’s B2B brand customers access to audio editing and show notes alongside hosting. For the Partnerships Lead, this offers a potential complementary service rather than asking Transistor to buy production services for itself.
hypotheses: Some B2B brands using Transistor may want outside help editing episodes and preparing show notes.
The Partnerships Lead may be open to referring customers to a specialist production provider.
strategy.angle: With Transistor powering branded podcasts for Kit.com, would an audio-editing and show-notes referral partner be useful for your B2B customers?
strategy.fit_reason: The service complements podcast hosting, and Transistor has confirmed branded-podcast customers. A customer referral partnership is plausible, although demand for production support and interest in such partnerships are unconfirmed.

draft.subject: Branded podcast support
draft.body:
Hi — I noticed Transistor powers branded podcasts for Kit.com.

I help B2B brands with podcast audio editing and show notes. If some of your customers want a little help turning episodes around, a referral partner might be a simple add-on for your team.

Would you be the right person to ask about a possible referral relationship for branded-show customers?
